public_rationale: The claim is a first-person report: Zitron says he 'can find no compelling evidence' that even a gigawatt of compute was available for Anthropic to buy. What he found and what he finds compelling cannot be checked, and he does not say when the gigawatt should have existed. His description of the NYT report holds for the 5GW figure (e1). Public company statements before the post do point to gigawatt-scale capacity: Google TPU capacity 'well over a gigawatt' expected in 2026 (e2), over a million Trainium2 chips in use, and nearly 1GW more from Amazon by end of 2026 (e3). But these are mostly plans or company claims without verified gigawatt totals, which is the kind of evidence he discounts. Grading the claim would require substituting a standard and a date he did not give.
limitations: Did not read the NYT original or the SpaceX Colossus coverage.
Company announcements are forward-looking and not independently verified.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Zitron can find no compelling evidence that there was even a gigawatt of compute available for Anthropic to buy, despite New York Times-reported investor statements that it would have 5GW by the end of 2026.

statement.excerpt: For example, the New York Times reported that Anthropic would have 5GW of capacity by the end of 2026, up from 1.5GW at the end of 2025, according to statements made to its investors, but I can find no compelling evidence that there was even a gigawatt of compute for it to buy.

from_speaker: the New York Times reported that Anthropic would have 5GW of capacity by the end of 2026, up from 1.5GW at the end of 2025
according to statements made to its investors
I can find no compelling evidence
that there was even a gigawatt of compute for it to buy
our_interpretation: The core claim reports the speaker's own search ('I can find no') against his own standard ('compelling'). Nobody else can check what he found or what he would find compelling.

The referent of 'there was even a gigawatt of compute for it to buy' is unclear. It could mean new compute available in 2026 to grow from 1.5GW toward 5GW, or compute existing at end of 2025. He gives no date.
The part about the NYT report can be checked. A summary of the NYT report confirms the 5GW end-of-2026 figure told to investors. The 1.5GW end-2025 figure was not found in the summary.
Earlier reviewers found that swapping in an objective public-evidence test with a fixed end-2025 date was unfair to the speaker. This contract does not do that.
criteria.support_condition: The claim would be supported if it were shown that no credible public evidence existed of at least a gigawatt of compute available to Anthropic. But 'compelling' is the speaker's own standard, and the time referent is unclear.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The claim would be contradicted if credible, verified evidence showed at least a gigawatt of compute actually available for Anthropic to buy at the time he means. Company forward-looking statements are what he discounts, and the time referent is unclear, so no clean test exists.

evidence.explanation: A public company statement that more than a gigawatt of Google TPU capacity was expected for Anthropic in 2026. It is a forward-looking plan, not proof of delivered capacity. Whether it counts as 'compelling' is the speaker's call.
